extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art history; practicing painters/sculptors and general educated readers interested in Renaissance/Tuscan art
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and qualities used to judge/describe 14th-century Tuscan painters and sculptors (drawing, composition, colour, invention, craftsmanship, media mastery, reputation). Useful for assessing works and careers of early Renaissance artists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence / industry of the artist
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter's constant labor and diligence in workmanship (e.g., 'he had no peer in diligence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari repeatedly praises industry as a central virtue: small works receive as much care as larger ones; diligence enables pioneers to overcome difficult problems. Example: Stefano's shrine painted 'with so much diligence that the work, small as it is, deserves to be praised no less than ... larger and more masterly' works. Implies that conscientious, sustained effort elevates technical achievement and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility in draughtsmanship / drawing skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability and ease in drawing—accurate line, good proportions and expressive draftsmanship (e.g., 'great facility in draughtsmanship').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by surviving drawings and frescoes (Vasari cites Stefano's drawing of the Transfiguration). Compared directly to masters (Stefano 'drew much better than Giotto' in Vasari's view). Good draughtsmanship underpins figure quality and expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivacity / lifelikeness of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A sense of liveliness and animation in figures and faces (e.g., 'vivacity never displayed up to that time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari values figures that feel alive — animated heads, vivid little figures in predellas, and lively attitudes. He cites scenes with varied ages and expressive attitudes as evidence of superior vivacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and specificity of physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Varied, believable portrayal of ages and individual faces (e.g., 'beautiful variety in the faces of the young, the men of middle age, and the old').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged by the artist's ability to differentiate age groups and character types within crowds or choirs; variety contributes to naturalism and narrative clarity (example: the circle of saints with distinct young, middle-aged, and old faces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and blending of colour
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour that is harmonious, mellow and well blended (e.g., 'more harmonious, more mellow, and better blended in colouring than all the others').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour is evaluated for subtlety and unity across a work. Vasari credits painters who achieve a mellow, well-blended palette as superior to contemporaries whose colouring is harsher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention / variety of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and variety in compositional invention (e.g., 'more varied in invention').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by novelty of scenes, poses, figure-grouping and narrative solutions. Vasari praises those who introduce new mannerisms or subject treatments that enrich the tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill with foreshortening and tackling difficult problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to attempt and develop foreshortening and other difficult representational problems, even if imperfect at first (e.g., 'those foreshortenings that he made...showed a faulty manner...none the less he who is the pioneer ... deserves a much greater name').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari rewards innovation and courage in solving hard pictorial problems; early imperfect attempts are still valuable if they open a new path for others. Being a pioneer in technique can count positively despite technical flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition, gesture and symbolic appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangement of figures, gestures, and symbols appropriate to subject and narrative (e.g., 'choir of angels ... appropriately carrying theological symbols ... all turned towards a Christ on the Cross').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by coherence of figure-grouping, directional focus, and meaningful use of attributes/symbols; successful compositions guide attention and reinforce theological or narrative points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for scale and grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to work on a grand scale and impart majesty (e.g., making Apostles 'each four braccia high' to give 'grandness to the manner').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by handling of large-scale frescoes, monumental figures and overall architectural integration; judged by the sense of majesty and appropriate scale relative to setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery across media (painting, sculpture, bronze casting, architecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competence in multiple related media: painting, sculpture, bronze founding, and architectural design (e.g., Andrea Pisano's excellence in casting in bronze and architecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari counts versatility as a major virtue — artists who succeed in sculptural reliefs, bronze doors, and architectural models are esteemed. Examples: Andrea's bronze door, shrine, marble statues, and architectural designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and intelligent use of antique models
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of classical antiquities and study of ancient examples to improve form and expression (e.g., antiquities in Pisa gave Andrea 'such great assistance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recovery and imitation of good ancient practice (proportions, nudes, expressions) is presented as a source of improvement; knowledge of different regional manners (Egyptian, Greek, Roman) informs judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to learn from masters and then improve upon them
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting a master's method (Giotto) and surpassing it in harmony, invention, or colour (e.g., Pietro Laurati 'imitated the manner of Giotto' and later 'became a better master').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari values assimilation plus innovation: following a great model but introducing improvements that advance the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweetness of manner and expressive harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: A pleasing, sweet style and harmonious expression in holy figures and angels (e.g., 'a very sweet manner in these blessed spirits, with such great harmony').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged by the emotional tone and unity of expression across a sacred subject; contributes to devotional effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish/polish and use of materials (gilding, polishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to finish and surface treatment, including polishing and gilding (e.g., bronze door 'made smooth and polished all over, but also gilded by fire').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of finish and appropriate material techniques (gilding, polish) enhance perceived excellence and suitability for prestigious commissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill in drapery and the depiction of cloth
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of draping and how garments confer majesty and naturalism (e.g., figures 'so beautifully adorned, so well draped, and so simply wrapped').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drapery should convey form beneath, lend dignity to figures, and be executed with grace; praised when it contributes to the noble bearing of heads and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liveliness and effectiveness in small-scale narrative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to render little figures and predella-scenes with vividness and narrative clarity (e.g., 'little figures so lively and so vivid ... it was something marvellous').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to animate miniature episodes is a distinct technical and compositional skill; success in small-scale work complements large-scale projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation, patronage and commissions as indicators of merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Being widely sought after, summoned by patrons, and commissioned for major public works (e.g., 'he was summoned...he was commissioned to make...') is treated as evidence of excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari treats frequent commissions, civic honors, and public placement of works (church altars, doors, façades) as corroborating the artist's technical and moral merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait likeness and the depiction of identifiable individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to render portraits and likenesses (e.g., 'the portrait of Messer Cino himself in marble').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and character in portraits—especially when incorporated into tombs, teaching scenes or altarpieces—are seen as signs of technical mastery and observational skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural design competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in architectural planning and designing civic/fortified structures and church models (e.g., Andrea's models for the Castle of Scarperia, Church of S. Giovanni at Pistoia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged by viability and elegance of designs, practical improvements to urban fabric, and successful realization or influence on built works.
